text_html: An epidemiologic study is conducted concerning the autosomal recessive form of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease in North America. In parts of Canada, the incidence of this disease is 1/900. Which of the following best represents the frequency of carriers in this population?
explanation_html:
Educational Objective: In autosomal recessive disease, incidence equals q² and carrier frequency is approximately 2q for rare alleles.

Key Concept: An incidence of 1/900 corresponds to q² = 1/900, so q = 1/30. For rare conditions, p equals approximately 1, making the carrier frequency 2q = 1/15.

Explanation: Using the Hardy-Weinberg law, the frequency of an autosomal recessive disease is represented by q², while carriers are represented by 2pq. When the disease allele is rare, p is approximately 1, allowing carrier frequency to be estimated simply as 2q after taking the square root of the disease incidence.

Differential: Because the disease incidence equals q², an incidence of 1/900 gives q = 1/30, and for rare autosomal recessive traits the carrier frequency is approximately 2q = 1/15.

Incorrect Answers: A, B, C, and E.

Choice A: 1/3 is incorrect. This implies q = 1/6 and a disease incidence of 1/36.

Choice B: 1/9 is incorrect. This implies q = 1/18 and a disease incidence of 1/324.

Choice C: 1/10 is incorrect. This implies q = 1/20 and a disease incidence of 1/400.

Choice A: 1/3 is incorrect. This implies q = 1/6 and a disease incidence of 1/36.

Choice B: 1/9 is incorrect. This implies q = 1/18 and a disease incidence of 1/324.

Choice C: 1/10 is incorrect. This implies q = 1/20 and a disease incidence of 1/400.

Choice E: 1/30 is incorrect. This represents the allele frequency q, not the carrier frequency, which would be approximately 2q = 1/15.
